analysis.title: GS Curtin - GS Rates MarketStrats | Are higher yields beginning to cause cracks?
key_insights: Higher terminal rates and term premia have pushed yield curves higher, and stress is emerging in issuers with large debt outstanding and heavy projected borrowing needs.

In sovereign markets, OAT spreads widened significantly, causing position stopouts and a shift to the EUR sovereign crisis playbook at the height of the stress: Schatz spreads widened, sovereign credit curves flattened, banks underperformed and the euro weakened.

In credit, stress points are showing in financing of the AI infrastructure buildout, particularly among neoclouds such as Coreweave. Hyperscaler all-in USD 10y debt cost of roughly 6-8% may be manageable if projected returns are in the teens or higher, but sub-investment grade borrowers feel higher yields more quickly.

GS has argued that resilient nominal growth plus heavy duration supply would keep pressuring yields higher, and that the strongest circuit breakers are fiscal consolidation and a pullback in AI capex intentions.

Measures to control DV01 supply (WAM reduction, buybacks, slower QT) have had positive but limited effects on term premium. Hawkish central banks in September should compress inflation risk premium, but front-end forwards like SFR M7-M8 have only flattened recently, as the Nasdaq has fallen.
The upcoming QRA could test this again if the US Treasury reduces long-end coupon supply.

If fiscal looseness or capex funding changes in investors' eyes, rates can rally meaningfully. GS is sceptical of fiscal consolidation and does not expect 2027 European elections to change the picture.

On AI, compute remains scarce and larger balance sheets may ease funding pressure along the supply chain. The pressure comes from the cost and scale of financing the build-out, not from compressed expected returns on invested capital.

The main European tail risk is energy, especially natural gas. Sam Dart and colleagues see meaningful upside risk to TTF if Hormuz flows do not improve and winter is 1 standard deviation colder or less windy. Central banks have pushed back on another round of tightening this month, guiding to a gradual pace.
This makes the risk-reward on curve steepeners out to 30y uncertain in spot space, as energy and AI sentiment compete for influence, with Dutch transition flows in the background.

GS concludes that markets will struggle to hold terminal rates at clearly restrictive levels because it is causing cracks in bond markets, and likes intermediate forwards such as 2y2y for asymmetry if higher terminal rates quickly weaken risk assets.

Energy upside scenario: central banks get pulled into tightening and second-round effects are priced, but terminal pricing would not hold as growth damage is priced in quickly. Z7-Z9 should flatten, with potential for greens/blues to rally outright.
AI worries scenario: if AI capex pace is re-evaluated, yield curves shift lower on weaker nominal growth and lower supply term premium, and rates rally.

Status quo scenario: if AI capex continues and the market holds term premium against higher 2027 inflation risk, 2y2y forwards will struggle to rally until there is more confidence in an inflation top. At 3.40% in EUR (3.20% in Estr), pricing is still 100bps above pre-Iran and 20bps below the September highs.

September was a bruising month for rates, and receiving 2y2y was caught in the risk reduction wave. GS sees this as a signal the position is less crowded, and with lower risk appetite argues for taking some risk outright or in bounded non-linear structures.
GS also likes long forwards in real yield space to add inflation protection against rising energy prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher terminal rates are causing cracks in bond markets and credit, so terminal rates will struggle to hold. This favours intermediate forwards like 2y2y, and rates can rally if fiscal looseness or AI capex funding changes.
tension_points.bear_case: If AI capex continues and the market holds term premium against higher inflation into 2027, 2y2y forwards will struggle to rally until there is more confidence in an inflation top. GS is also sceptical of fiscal consolidation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued status quo of AI capex plus inflation risk into 2027 would stall the 2y2y rally. An energy leg higher pulling central banks into tightening would also challenge the view in the near term.
